note.explanation: Ionic compounds have no overall charge. Write the cation and anion with their charges, then use the crisscross method: cross the numerical charge values to become subscripts and drop the charge signs. For example, Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃. If both subscripts have a common factor, reduce them to the simplest whole-number ratio.
note.simple: Match the total positive charge with the total negative charge. Cross the charge numbers to make subscripts, then remove the signs.
note.checkQuestion: What formula is formed from Mg²⁺ and N³⁻?
note.title: Writing formulas for ionic compounds
steps: Write the cation and its charge first.
Write the anion and its charge next.
Cross the numerical values of the charges to become subscripts.
Drop the charge signs and write the resulting formula.
Check that the compound is electrically neutral.

mcqs.stem: What is the formula of the ionic compound formed from Na⁺ and Cl⁻?
rationales: NaCl is correct because one positive charge balances one negative charge.
Na₂Cl has an unbalanced total charge of +1.
NaCl₂ has an unbalanced total charge of −1.
Na₂Cl₂ is electrically neutral but its subscripts reduce to the simplest ratio, NaCl.

mcqs.stem: Which formula is formed from Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻?
rationales: CaCl does not balance the +2 charge on calcium.
CaCl₂ is correct because two chloride ions balance one calcium ion.
Ca₂Cl has an unbalanced total charge.
Ca₂Cl₂ is electrically neutral but reduces to the simplest ratio CaCl₂.

mcqs.stem: What is the formula of the compound formed from Al³⁺ and O²⁻?
rationales: AlO does not balance the +3 and −2 charges.
Al₂O has a total charge of +4.
AlO₃ has a total charge of −3.
Al₂O₃ is correct because two Al³⁺ ions and three O²⁻ ions have equal total charges.

mcqs.stem: Choose the correct formula for a compound formed from Mg²⁺ and N³⁻.
rationales: MgN does not balance the charges.
Mg₂N₃ has a total charge of −5.
Mg₃N₂ is correct because three Mg²⁺ ions balance two N³⁻ ions.
MgN₂ has a total charge of −4.

mcqs.stem: What is the simplest formula for the compound formed from K⁺ and O²⁻?
rationales: K₂O is correct because two K⁺ ions balance one O²⁻ ion.
KO has a total charge of −1.
KO₂ has a total charge of −3.
K₂O₂ is neutral but reduces to the simplest ratio K₂O.

mcqs.stem: Which formula is formed from Ba²⁺ and N³⁻?
rationales: BaN does not balance the charges.
BaN₂ has a total charge of −4.
Ba₂N₃ has a total charge of −5.
Ba₃N₂ is correct because three Ba²⁺ ions balance two N³⁻ ions.

mcqs.stem: What is the simplest formula for the compound formed from Zn²⁺ and Br⁻?
rationales: ZnBr does not balance zinc's +2 charge.
ZnBr₂ is correct because two Br⁻ ions balance one Zn²⁺ ion.
Zn₂Br has a total charge of +3.
Zn₂Br₂ is neutral but reduces to the simplest ratio ZnBr₂.

mcqs.stem: Which formula is formed from Li⁺ and O²⁻?
rationales: LiO has a total charge of −1.
Li₂O is correct because two Li⁺ ions balance one O²⁻ ion.
LiO₂ has a total charge of −3.
Li₂O₂ is neutral but reduces to the simplest ratio Li₂O.

written.text: Write down the chemical formulas of the following compounds. Calcium phosphate, Aluminium nitride, Sodium acetate, Ammonium carbonate and Bismuth sulphate.

rubric.why: Calcium phosphate requires the correct ratio of the ions.
rubric.description: Give the formula of calcium phosphate.
rubric.how: Use Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ to obtain Ca₃(PO₄)₂.

rubric.why: Aluminium nitride has a one-to-one ion ratio.
rubric.description: Give the formula of aluminium nitride.
rubric.how: Use Al³⁺ and N³⁻ to obtain AlN.

rubric.why: The sodium and acetate ions must be represented in a neutral formula.
rubric.description: Give the formula of sodium acetate.

rubric.why: The final formulas must show the correct ratios for both remaining compounds.

modelAnswer: Calcium phosphate: Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂
Aluminium nitride: Al³⁺ and N³⁻ → AlN
Sodium acetate: Na⁺ and C₂H₃O₂⁻ → NaC₂H₃O₂
Bismuth sulphate: Bi³⁺ and SO₄²⁻ → Bi₂(SO₄)₃

examTips: This topic is commonly tested by asking you to write a formula from the name of an ionic compound or from the ions and their charges.
For a short-answer formula question, show the ions and their charges, then show the crisscross step and final formula.
Marks are earned for using the correct ion charges and for giving subscripts that make the compound electrically neutral.
Use the smallest whole-number ratio of ions in the final formula.

yourTurn.question: Write down the chemical formulas of the following compounds. Calcium phosphate, Aluminium nitride, Sodium acetate, Ammonium carbonate and Bismuth sulphate.
solution: Calcium phosphate: Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻; crisscross to give Ca₃(PO₄)₂.
Aluminium nitride: Al³⁺ and N³⁻; the ratio is 1:1, so the formula is AlN.
Sodium acetate: Na⁺ and C₂H₃O₂⁻; the ratio is 1:1, so the formula is NaC₂H₃O₂.
Ammonium carbonate: NH₄⁺ and CO₃²⁻; crisscross to give (NH₄)₂CO₃.
Bismuth sulphate: Bi³⁺ and SO₄²⁻; crisscross to give Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

explain.title: Start with the ions
explain.body: In order to write down the formula of an ionic compound, first identify the cations and anions and the number of charges present on them. Finally combine the two ions together to form an electrically neutral compound.

explain.title: Use the ion charges
explain.body: If you know the name of binary ionic compound, you can write its chemical formula. Start by writing symbol of cation with its charge. Then write the symbol of anion with its charge and find out how many of these ions are needed to give an electrically neutral compound.

explain.title: Apply the crisscross method
explain.body: Let us now apply crisscross method to write the formula. In this method, the numerical value of each of the ion charges is crossed over to become the subscript of the other ion. Signs of the charges are then dropped.

explain.title: Check the final formula
explain.body: The compound must be electrically neutral. For Al₂O₃, two Al³⁺ ions give a total charge of +6 and three O²⁻ ions give a total charge of −6.

mistakes: Writing the charge signs as part of the final compound formula.
Putting a charge value under the same ion instead of crossing it to the other ion.
Forgetting to check that the total positive and negative charges balance.
Writing a ratio that can be reduced instead of the simplest whole-number ratio.
Leaving out parentheses when a polyatomic ion needs a subscript, such as writing NH₄₂ instead of (NH₄)₂.
